headline: Big 5 Global returns to Dubai in November with nine Co-located shows
deck: The co-location structure is the thing to plan around: nine specialist shows under one roof means a buyer covers categories that used to take three trips.
excerpt: Big 5 Global runs from 23 to 26 November at the Dubai World Trade Centre, with more than 2,800 exhibitors expected and nine co-located specialist events. Programme themes include 3D concrete printing, digital twins and passive cooling.
content:
Big 5 Global returns to the Dubai World Trade Centre from 23 to 26 November, with organisers expecting more than 2,800 exhibitors and over 85,000 attendees from upwards of 165 countries.

The structure of the event, rather than its size, is what determines how it is worth using. Big 5 Global runs alongside nine co-located specialist shows: Heavy, Totally Concrete, Marble & Stone World, Urban Design & Landscape, Windows Doors & Facades, HVACR World, LiveableCitiesX, GeoWorld and FutureFM. A contractor sourcing across structure, envelope, services and facilities management covers in one visit what previously required several. GeoWorld, the ground engineering show, and FutureFM, the facilities management one, bracket that sequence: the ground under a building at one end and the contract that runs it at the other, which is the span the Riyadh edition covers with Heavy Saudi Arabia and Saudi FM & Clean.

That matters most for the categories that sit between disciplines. Facade procurement touches glazing, sealants, thermal performance and the structural fixing behind it, and those have historically been exhibited in different places. Co-location puts the specification conversation and the supply conversation in the same building.

The programme themes organisers have set out — sustainable construction, 3D concrete printing, building information modelling and digital twins, Gulf giga-projects, and passive cooling — indicate where the show expects buyer attention. Passive cooling is the one most specific to the region: reducing cooling load through orientation, shading, thermal mass and envelope performance addresses the largest single component of building energy use in the Gulf, and it is a design decision rather than an equipment purchase.

Three-dimensional concrete printing occupies a different position. It has moved from demonstration toward limited production use in the region, and the constraint has been less the printing than the surrounding system: mix design that holds shape while remaining pumpable, reinforcement strategies that satisfy code, and inspection regimes for a process that has no conventional formwork record.

The 46th edition of the show concluded in Dubai in November 2025. The event sits in a regional calendar that now includes a substantial Saudi edition, and the two serve different functions — the Riyadh show is closer to the kingdom's own procurement, while the Dubai event remains the larger international gathering and the one where suppliers outside the region make first contact with Gulf buyers.

For manufacturers considering the show, the practical planning question is which of the co-located events a target buyer actually walks. A visitor sourcing HVAC equipment may never reach the stone hall. Exhibitor placement within the co-location structure does more to determine useful conversations than stand size does.

Registration and programme details are published by the organisers ahead of the event.
